Pre 1 · Group 06 (Questions 101-120) · Card 102 · Original Q45 Regarding the effects of MRI scanning: A RF fields can cause peripheral nerve stimulation B Equipment leads exposed to
Card 102 · Original Q45
Regarding the effects of MRI scanning:
ARF fields can cause peripheral nerve stimulation
BEquipment leads exposed to the gradient field can cause skin burns if inappropriately positioned
CIntraorbital metal fragments are of concern primarily because they can become overheated and cause thermal damage to the retina
DStaff with body piercings must wear lead-lined undergarments when approaching the magnet
EWith a SAR of 1.0, the patient’s body temperature will rise by more than 0.5°C if they are scanned for 30 min
إظهار الإجابة
Card 102 · Original Q45
Regarding the effects of MRI scanning:
ARF fields can cause peripheral nerve stimulation
BEquipment leads exposed to the gradient field can cause skin burns if inappropriately positioned
CIntraorbital metal fragments are of concern primarily because they can become overheated and cause thermal damage to the retina
DStaff with body piercings must wear lead-lined undergarments when approaching the magnet
EWith a SAR of 1.0, the patient’s body temperature will rise by more than 0.5°C if they are scanned for 30 min
Answer
AFalse — RF fields can cause peripheral nerve stimulation
(Peripheral nerve stimulation is caused by changing gradient fields, not RF fields)
BFalse — Equipment leads exposed to the gradient field can cause skin burns if inappropriately positioned
(Burns occur due to RF heating when cables or metal touch the skin, not because of the gradient field)
CFalse — Intraorbital metal fragments are of concern primarily because they can become overheated and cause thermal damage to the retina
(The main concern is that metal fragments may move or rotate due to the magnetic field, causing tissue damage—not overheating)
DFalse — Staff with body piercings must wear lead-lined undergarments when approaching the magnet
(All ferromagnetic materials must be removed; lead does not prevent magnetic attraction)
EFalse — With a SAR of 1.0, the patient’s body temperature will rise by more than 0.5°C if they are scanned for 30 min
(A SAR of 1.0 should not raise body temperature by more than 0.5°C during a 30-minute scan)

don’t cause vasoconstriction. Can cause pain and burning sensation.

Question 46 The purpose of using personal monitoring device is to
Aprotect the radiologist from radiation. (It is used to monitor the amount of radiation exposed to personnel and not to protect the radiation worker from radiation. )

Dindicate an occupational exposure. (Personal monitoring device should be worn by radiation workers in every procedure related to radiation exposure.)
Erecognise the type of radiation received by personnel (Filters in personal dosimeters help in identifying the type of radiation received.)

Original text & correction
geiger-Muller counter used for radiation survey
Ahas a thick window to detect alpha particle. (. Thicker window will absorb alpha particle and resulted in the alpha particle being undetected in the gas.)
Bhas low efficiency in detecting gamma radiation. (Detection efficiency for gamma radiation is lower than alpha or beta particles as the radiation is more penetrating.)
Cis a dosimeter-type detector. (The detector is a counter-type detector)
Ddistinguishes beta particle from alpha particle. (Different window thickness can be used to distinguish alpha and beta particles. Beta detection requires thicker window to absorb alpha particle. )
Erequires a multichannel analyser to read out the signal from radiation interaction (The counter cannot distinguish energy and doesn’t require multichannel analyser to differentiate the energy)

Pre 2 · Exam 05 · Pre 2 · Card 90 Patient preparation for CT cardiac
Pre 2 · Card 90
Patient preparation for CT cardiac
إظهار الإجابة
Pre 2 · Card 90
Patient preparation for CT cardiac
Answer
Original text & correction
Patient preparation for CT cardiac 1. Avoid caffeine – this includes tea, coffee and caffeine-containing soft drinks (including ‘decaffeinated’ varieties), ‘energy’ pills and Viagra-type medication 24 hr before exam 2. Drugs – patients should take all their normal cardiac medication as usual on the day of the test. 3. Thorough explanation of the procedure to the patient aids compliance, particularly with regard to breath-hold (suggest patient takes a ‘3/4 breath’ when instructed – less likely to move during scan and avoids ‘Valsalva’ manoeuvre affecting contrast bolus entering chest). 4. 18G cannula in right antecubital fossa – siting cannula in right arm reduces artefact as contrast crosses the mediastinum. For graft studies this avoids streak artefact obscuring origin of LIMA grafts. 5. Assess suitability for administration of β-blockers and sublingual nitrates

Question 53 the plane of probe when you do biopsy When performing a biopsy, the plane of the probe or needle in relation to the ultrasound probe is critical for accurate targeting. Out-of-plane approach: o In this method, the needle is inserted perpendicular to the ultrasound probe • The needle is never oblique at any methods .

Dbarium should be infused at a rate of approximately 75 ml/min.

Answer
Answer
AFalse - Enteroclysis is not contraindicated in suspected small bowel obstruction. Barium will be diluted by thesmall intestinal fluid thus avoiding impaction.

CTrue - If the tip of the tube is in the jejunum then the risk of reflux of barium into the stomach is minimised.

ETrue - Too fast an infusion of barium may distend and paralyse the jejunum, resulting in delayed filling of ileal loops.

67. F. F. T. F. F.
The adrenal glands lie retroperitoneally above each kidney. Three arteries supply each gland, the superior, middle and inferior adrenal arteries these arise from the inferior phrenic, aorta and the renal arteries respectively. A single vein drains each adrenal gland. The right adrenal vein drains. into the IVC and the left to the left renal vein.

AAre generally safe to be injected directly into the patient

Pre 2 · Card 163
57. Radionuclides:
AAre generally safe to be injected directly into the patient
BIdeally emit alpha particles when used in a clinical setting
CFor medical use can be created locally in a cyclotron
DThat are isotopes of their parent nuclide are easily separated for clinical use
EAre not radioactive until they are injected into the patient
Answer
8a. False
Radionuclides are attached to pharmaceuticals to create compounds called radiopharmaceuticals. Ideally these should localize in the tissue of interest, be eliminated from the body with a half-life similar to the length of the study, and have a low toxicity.
8b. False
Alpha particles have a very short range in tissue, meaning they would not escape the patient; this would make detection difficult and transfer a very high dose to the patient. Ideally a radiopharmaceutical would emit gamma rays. 7. Radionuclide Imaging: Answers
8c. True
F-18 with a half-life of 110 min is produced this way.
8d. False As they are isotopes they have the same chemical and metabolic properties; this makes separation of a pure radionuclide difficult.
8e. False
They should always be handled with care, e.g. lead shielded containers and syringes, prepared behind a lead screen.
